caseno: Appeal from original Decree No. 165 of 1965
lawyer:
Anil Chandra Sarker -----For Appellant in F. A. No. 1 69 of 1965 and for respondent in F. A. No. 165. 
Nizamuddin Haider with A.B.M Abbasuddin -----For Respondent in F. A. No. 169 of 1965 and for Appellant in F.A. No. 165 of 1965.
parties:
Imanuddin Rarhi ----- Appellant in F A No 169 and Respondent in F.A. No. 165/65.
Vs.
Lilabati Das ----- Respondent in F.A. 169 and Appellant in F.A. No. 165/65.
case_source: Appeal against the judgment, order and Decree dated 23rd January 1965 passed by Mr. R. K. Biswas, Subordinate Judge of the First Court at Barisal, in Bakerganj in Title Suit No. 376 of 1963 of the said court declaring the decree in T. S. No. 449/69.
full_judgment:
Abdul Wadud Chowdhury J: These two appeals are directed against the judgment and decree passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, Barisal dated 23-1-1965 in Title Suit No. 367 of 1963 and arises out of a suit for declaration of the plaintiff's raiyat right in Kha schedule land as also for a further declaration that the ex-parte decree that was passed in Title Suit No. 449 of 1961 of the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge. Barisal, detailed in schedule 'Ka' of the plaint is void, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiff.
2. The Plaintiff's case to the effect that the suit properties described in 'Kha' schedule of the plaint was acquired by the plaintiff in the benami of Sudhendu Roy Chowdhury and Serala Sundari Basu by virtue of two pattas and Kabalas of different dates. The Plaintiff, however, took settlement of the suit land from Sudhendu Nath Roy Chowdhury by a patta dated 22nd Jaistha, 1348 BS corresponding to 5-9-35 AD in the name of Serala Sundari Basu. She paid selami of Rs. 475 for the patta. The plaintiff again took settlement of land from Sarala Sundari Basu in the benami of Sudhendu Nath Roy Chowdhury by a patta dated 19th Kartick, 1360 BS (5-11-53) and she paid the selami for the same. Both the pattas were in the custody of the plaintiff. After the said pattas Sarala Sundari sold her superior right to" the Plaintiff by a kabala dated 21st Kartick, 1360 BS (7-11-53) and the said kabala was taken in the benami of Sudhendu Nath Roy. Consideration money was paid by the Plaintiff. As such three documents were executed in the benami of Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari with the money and in the interest of the Plaintiff and Sudhendu Nath Roy and Sarala Sundari were mere name lenders of the Plaintiff being near relations of her. The Plaintiff thus acquired the suit property in the benami of Sudhendu Nath Roy and Sarala Sundari Basu. During the RS operation the suit properties were recorded in the name of the said two benamders at her instance. Subsequently since Sudhendu Nath Roy and Sarala Sundari did not execute any Nadabi Patia, she brought Title Suit No. 267 of 1960 before the Court of the Sub-ordinate Judge, Barisal for declaration of her title with respect to the disputed properties and obtained an ex-parte decree on 2-9-60. Thereafter, the Plaintiff got her name mutated in place of those persons before the acquired Estate and the name of the benamders were struck off from the settlement record. The Plaintiff later on came to know from her husband that the defendant obtained a decree in respect of 'Kha' schedule land in Title Suit No. 449 of 1961 of the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Barisal on 9-3-65 although the defendant No. 1 had no right, title or possession in the suit property. No summons of the said suit was served either on Sudhendu Nath Roy or Sarala Sundari Basu as those two persons were Indian citizens. As such, the alleged ex-parte decree is fraudulent and not binding on the plaintiff. The defendant No. 1 got the summons of the said suit served on one Mafizuddin alleging him to be Karmachari of Sudhendu Nath Roy and Sarala Sundari Basu though he was not so. The defendant has no title or possession in the suit properties and the story of settlement from Sudhendu Nath Roy and Sarala Sundari is false. There was no settlement of the suit properties by Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari in favour of defendant No. 1 and no possession was delivered to the defendant No. by them. As such the defendants did not acquire any title to the suit property by virtue of the said decree which is fraudulent. The plaintiff acquired right, title and interest in the suit property by virtue of her pattas and kabala and subsequently by virtue of her ex-parte decree obtained against Sudhendu Nath Roy and Sarala Sundari. In that view of the matter, the plaintiff has filed the present suit for declaration as above as a cloud has been cast upon the title of the plaintiff.
3. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form the plaintiff's story of acquiring of title on the basis, of said pattas and the Kabalas are denied by the defendant No. 1. He further contended that the said three documents were not benami transactions and neither Sudhendu Nath Roy nor Sarala Sundari was the benamider of the plaintiff. No consideration did pass at the instance of the plaintiff herself with regard to the said three documents. It was further contended by the Defendant that the plaintiff was never in possession of the suit properties and she acquired no title in the same as benamder of Sudhendu Nath Roy and Sarala Sundari. The defendant further contended that Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari acquired the suit properties in their own names with their own modify and the RS records were correctly prepared in their names. While thus in possession on the owners i.e. Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari settled the suit property with the defendants on 28th Chaitra 1360 BS at a jama of Rs. 15 and delivered possession to him. The defendant No. 1 is in possession of the suit land since the settlement in his favour. As SA Khatian did not record the name of the defendant in spite of his settlement he brought Title Suit No. 449 of 1961 before the court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Barisal against Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari and obtained a decree after due service of summons upon the said two persons. The said decree was bonafide and could not be called into question by the plaintiff. As Sudhendu Nath Roy and Sarala Sundari leased out the suit property to the defendant No. 1, the husband of the plaintiff subsequently obtained the original pattas and kabala clandestinely and brought Title Suit No; 267 of 1960 and obtained a fraudulent decree against Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari in respect of the suit property. Neither the plaintiff nor her husband ever posseted the suit property or realised any rent from tenants. The defendant further contended that the decree obtained by the defendant against Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari was bonafide and valid decree after due service of summons upon them at their Barisal residence. The husband of the plaintiff is the proprietor of the Sonali Cinema Hall. His business is to acquire properties of thereon resident Hindus and to prepare false and forged documents in his name from the aforesaid non-resident Hindus. It was further staged that the suit of the Plaintiff is hit by Ordinances I and VI of 1964 and the Plaintiff has no locus standi or any legal character to file the present suit.
4. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge dismissed the suit of the Plaintiff holding that the plaintiff could not prove her title by benami purchase in the name of Sudhendu Nath Roy and Sarala Sundari. He found that the ingredients of benami have not been proved. He also found that the plaintiff's ex-parte decree in Title Suit No. 267 of 1960, the sheet anchor of the plaintiff's title, was tinged with fraud in view of the fact that though the defendants of that suit i.e. Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari were not in the then Pakistan and were Indian citizen yet notices were served upon them at Barisal through one Daruba Nath PW 3. Though Daruba Nath has admitted that he had no interest in the suit proper-ties yet he was made a defendant in the said suit. In that view of the matter, he found that the plaintiff did not acquire the suit properties in the benami of Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari. He also found that the decree obtained by the plaintiff in the Title Suit No 267 of 1960 against Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari. In respect of the suit properties is nothing but fraudulent and, as such, the plaintiff has got no title in the 'Kha' schedule properties and the case of benami has not been proved. He has, however, found that the plaintiff has proved his present possession from the time of the ex-parte decree obtained by him. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge after deciding that the plaintiff has no title or interest in the suit land and that the ex-parte decree obtained by him against Sudhendu Nath and Sarala were fraudulent, also considered the decrees obtained by the defendant No. 1 was also fraudulent and collusive as such he dismissed the suit of the plaintiff with the finding that the ex-parte decree passed in Title Suit Nos. 449 of 1961 and 267 of 1960 of that court was also declared to be null and void. As against the said judgment and decree passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, both the plaintiff and the defendant No. 1 preferred two appeals. The plaintiff's appeal is FA No. 169 of 1965 and the defendant's appeal is FA No. 165 of 1965. The Plaintiff's appeal was against the dismissal of his case as also against the declaration that his ex-parte decree in Title Suit No. 267 of 1960 was fraudulent and null and void. The delft's appeal was against the findings of the learned Sub-ordinate Judge that the Title Suit No. 449 of 1061 obtained by him against Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari was fraudulent and, as such, null and void. As these two appeals arise out of the same judgment and decree and is with regard to the same suit land we dispose of both these appeals by this judgment.
5. Mr Anil Chandra Sarkar appeared on behalf of the plaintiff appellant in FA No. 169 of 1965 and Mr. Nizamuddin Haider with Mr. ABM Abbasuddin appeared on behalf of the defendant No. 1 appellant in FA No. 165 of 1965. Mr Anil Chandra Sarker learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the Plaintiff appellant in FA No. 169 of 1965, submits that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge erred in law and against the weight of evidence on record in holding that the plaintiff has not been able to-prove her title by benami purchase. He then submits that the trial court should not have decided the propriety or otherwise of the ex-parte decree passed in favour of the plaintiff in Title, Suit No. 267 of 1960 in view of the fact that no specific issue has been raised as regard the said decree and no particulars of fraud have been alleged in the written statement and no evidence of fraud have been given by the defendant. He further submits that the said ex parte decree ought to have been accepted by the court below as valid. He also submits that the benami character of the suit land cannot be set-aside without setting aside the ex-parte decree and the ex-parte decree cannot be act aside at the instance of the defendant No. 1 who could not challenge it because he was not a party to the said suit Mr Sarkar learned Advocate further urged that in view of the finding of possession arrived at by the trial court he is entitled to a declaration to the effect that the defendant's decree was fraudulent and void. Mr Nizamuddin Haider the learned Advocate, on the other hand, submits that the trial court's findings so far as the question of benami and declaration to the effect that the plaintiffs ex parte decree was fraudulent are based on sound principle of law and should be maintained but so far as the decree declaring the defendant's decree in Title Suit No. 449 of 1961, to be fraudulent and null and void is not maintainable in view of the fact that the plaintiff is to succeed on his own case and she having failed to prove her title in the suit property. She has no legal character and as such she is not entitled to any such declaration that the decree obtained by the defendant was forged, null and void. As regards the first point urged by Mr Sarker that he has been able to prove benami character of the said documents. We find from the judgment of the court below that he has considered about the benami character of those documents. He has found out that the plaintiff had no relationship with Sudhendu Nath & Sarala Sundari. He also found that there is no evidence of payment by the plaintiff of the consideration money. As regards the custody of the document the learned Sub-ordinate Judge has found that those documents came into possession of the plaintiff in connection with the purchase of land from a co-sharers of Sudhendu Nath i.e. Defendant No. 2, Jatindra Nath Roy the brother of Sudhendu Nath Roy. He also found that that the Plaintiff could not prove any motive for the said alleged benami transactions. We have considered the evidence on record; we do not find that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge has committed any error in coming to such finding. We also, on consideration of evidence on record, find that the plaintiff has not been able to prove the ingredients of benami. In that view of the matter the learned sub-ordinate Judge was correct in holding that the plaintiff had no right, title and interest in the suit land. In the light of the said finding it was necessary for the court to come into the question as to how the ex-parte decree was obtained by the plaintiff in Title Suit No. 267 of 1960. The plaintiff claimed title, by virtue of benami purchase and the ex-parte decree. The ex-parte decree was obtained on the basis of the benami. So when it has been found that the plaintiff could not prove benami character of the transacting it could not be said that the ex-parte decree has any leg to stand upon. In order to find out whether the plaintiff had any right, title and interest in the suit land, the consideration as to whether the said-decree was validly obtained or not was necessary. It cannot be said that since the decree has been passed in Title Suit No. 267 of 1960 the court cannot go into the question of the validity of the decree. In order to arrive at a finding as to whether the Plaintiff had any right, title or interest in the kha schedule property the court has of necessity to go into the question of the question of the genuineness of the ex-parte decree and to Come to a finding whether the same was a valid decree or not. In that view of the matter the objection taken by the learned Advocate for the appellant that since no issue has been raised on the quest ion of validity of the said ex-parte decree the same could not be considered by the trial count and the decree cannot be set aside. We are unable or accept the said contention of the learned Advocate for the appellant. The court was within his province in sifting the evidence or record as to whether the ex-parte decree was genuine or tinged with fraud. It is of no consequence whether the defendant raised any objection with regard to the said ex-parte decree. The Plaintiff was to prove her case and in proving heir case she has to adduce evidence as to whether the said decree which was the sheet-anchor of her title was valid or not. When the court on consideration of the facts, circumstances and evidence led in the case came to the conclusion that the transfers were genuine and not benami and the plaintiff did not acquire the property in the benami of Sudhendra Nath and Sarala Sundari, obviously it has to see whether the ex-parte decree obtained on the basis of the said allegation of benami has legs to stand upon. So we do not find any illegality in the findings of the learned Sub-ordinate Judge in considering the genuineness of the ex-parte decree. In that view of the matter we do not find any sub-stance in the argument advanced by the learned Advocate for the appellant that the decree could not be assailed or set-aside by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge in the present suit. Moreover, the evidence on record discussed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge as discussed in the judgment tends to show that the decree obtained in Title Suit No. 267 of 1960 was fraudulently obtained because of the fact that though there is evidence on record to the effect that Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari were Indian citizens and were not living in the then East Pakistan for a long time, curiously enough the summons were served on them at Barisal through PW 3 Daruba Nath. This Dhruba Nath was made party in that suit though he admitted in his deposition here that he had no interest whatsoever in the suit land and Dhruba Nath PW 3 was an employee of the husband of the plaintiff. This alone is enough to come to a finding that the decree was fraudulent. It has been argued by Mr Sarkar, the learned Advocate that since no fraud has been alleged by the defendant the court suo motu could not go into that question and set-aside the decree. But as we have stated earlier, the genuineness or otherwise of the said decree was very much in issue in deciding the title of the plaintiff as it was found that the plaintiff could not prove benami character-of the documents. In that view the nature and character of the ex-parte decree required scrutiny and the court on scrutinising the same has found that the said decree was obtained fraudulently. We do not find any illegality in the treatment of the case by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge on this account.
6. Mr Sarker, the learned Advocate for the appellant has further submitted that in view of the fact that the court has found possession of the suit land with the plaintiff he had a legal character and he was entitled to a declaration that the defendant's decree was fraudulent and null and void. Let us now examine section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act is as follows:—
"Any person entitled to any legal character, or to any right as to any property, may institute a suit against any person denying or interested to deny, his title to such character or right, and the court may in its discretion make therein a declaration that he is so entitled and the plaintiff need not in such suit ask for any further relief; Provided that no court shall make any such declaration where the plaintiff being able to seek further relief than a mere declaration of title, omits to do so"
<u><u>7. The Plaintiff may ask for relief under that section provided that the plaintiff must at the time of the suit be entitled to any legal character or to any right to any property. Section 42 must be construed strictly. The courts are only to grant such declaration which came within the terms of that section where the plaintiff has asked for a declaratory decree, namely a declaration that the decree obtained was fraudulent and void. Such a simple declaration could not be given within the provisions; of section 42 as such the suit on the face of that section has to be dismissed. In the present case we find that the plaintiff could not prove her title to the suit land although the learned Sub-ordinate Judge has found that he was in possession of the same since the passing of the ex-parte decree in his favour. Mr Sarker, the Learned Advocate has referred to a decision of this court in the case of Aminul Islam vs M/s Kilburn & Co. reported in 18 DLR 691 where it has been held that if a possessor owner is wrongfully deprived of the thing by person other than the true owner he can recover khas possession of it, after evicting the defendant from the land on the basis of possessory title even if he has not acquired any valid title. The facts of that case are completely different from the present case. In the reported case the suit was filed under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act on the averment that the plaintiff was in possession and he has been subsequently dispossessed from the suit land on encroachment by the defendant. There it was held that thought the plaintiff did not acquire any valid title, he was entitled to recover khas possession. Of course, in that case the plaintiff acquired goodwill and all interest of the original owner by virtue of an agreement. In the agreement it was stated that consideration of the goodwill and the assets of the original owner passed to the plaintiff and he would be paid by allotment of shares. In consequence of that transaction they were in possession of the suit land. It was found that the original Company validly transferred the disputed land to the plaintiff till they were dispossessed by the defendant. It was found there that the plaintiff did not acquire valid title to the suit land as no instrument of transfer was effected between the plaintiff and the original owner. But in the context it was held that plaintiff was entitled to a decree for khas possession. But in the present case the plaintiff did not file any suit for khas possession or anything of that sort and there is also nothing to show that the owners of the land transferred the suit land in favour of the plaintiff. But on the other hand, it has been found by the court below as also by us that the plaintiff could riot prove the benami nature of the document. Rather the findings of the court below are to the effect that the plaintiff went into possession of the suit land after the passing of the ex-parte decree. In that view of the matter, the decision cited by Mr Sarker is of assistance to this case. The Plaintiff has prayed for a declaration to the effect that the decree obtained by the defendant was fraudulent and collusive and not binding against the plaintiff. The plaintiff having failed to prove her title and having no legal character in the subject matter of the suit land, was not entitled to any declaration with regard to the defendant's decree to which she had no connection. If however, it transpires from the evidence on record that the decree obtained by the defendant was also tainted with the same defect as that of the plaintiff though in the present suit. We do not hold that the plaintiff was entitled of any such declaration with regard to the defendant's decree since the matter is not before us. In the interest of justice we notice that the defendant No. 1's decree was also not in accordance with law, Summons of the suit was served on a person who had no interest in the suit and admittedly the defendants of that suit were Indian citizens, but their addresses in the suit were given to be in East Pakistan. From all these the learned Sub-ordinate Judge was correct in holding that the defendant's decree also suffers from the same defect as that of the Plaintiff. However, since the plaintiff has no locus standi to challenge the same and Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari were not parties in the present suit we do not declare in the present suit the defendant's decree to be a nullify. Another factor to be noticed in the present case was that Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari were impleaded as deft. Nos. 2 and 3 in the present suit but ultimately their names were struck off. The title to the suit land remained with Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari, as such, they having not been implicated, their names having been struck off; the learned Sub-ordinate Judge has correctly dismissed the suit holding that the present suit was not maintainable in the absence of the real owners.</u></u>
8. The result, therefore, is that the judgment and decree passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge dismissing the suit of the plaintiff are hereby affirmed the appeal No FA 169 of 1965 is hereby dismissed and the judgment and decree passed by the learned sub-ordinate Judge are affirmed. The appeal No FA 165 of 1965 is allowed with the observations made in the body of the judgments the parties will bear their respective costs.
End.
